extracted.intended_audience: U.S. institutions of higher education (universities) preparing white papers and full proposals for the FY25 Department of Defense MURI competition (ONR/ARO/AFOSR)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting white papers and full proposals to the FY25 DoD Multidisciplinary University Research Initiative (MURI) FOA, including following formatting, eligibility, compliance, and submission requirements and topic-specific constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper deadline and inquiry date
rubrics_metrics.description: White Papers must be received no later than 17 May 2024 at 5:00 PM Eastern Time. White Paper inquiries and questions due 03 May 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White papers are OPTIONAL but strongly recommended. Questions submitted after the Q&A deadline may not be answered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application deadline and Grants.gov validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be received no later than 06 September 2024 at 5:00 PM Eastern Time and must be ‘VALIDATED’ by Grants.gov by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation can take up to 48 hours after successful submission. It is strongly recommended that applications be submitted at least 2 business days ahead of the stated deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission pathways and portal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers and proposals have defined submission routes: white papers to ONR via FedConnect, to ARO via email/USPS/commercial carrier or as specified, to AFOSR via APAN link; full proposals must be submitted through Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT use the FedConnect message center to submit questions or responses to this announcement. Hard copy white papers should be stapled (no binders). Separate attachments (brochures, reprints) will not be accepted. Do NOT email ZIP files and/or password protected files.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper format (layout and font)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper size 8.5 x 11-inch; margins 1 inch; single-spaced; Times New Roman, 12-point; page limit no more than four (4) pages, single-sided (excluding cover letter, cover page, and CVs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: White paper pages beyond the 4-page limit may not be evaluated or read.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper required content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers shall include a cover sheet (FOA number, proposed title, proposer's technical POC with contact info, topic number and title) and provide: proposed technical approaches; potential impact on DoD capabilities; potential team and management plan; summary of estimated costs; CVs of key investigators; identification of any organizational conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ONR submissions use the specific cover sheet available on the ONR website. The white paper should provide sufficient information (hypothesis, theories, concepts, approaches, data measurements and analysis, etc.) to allow assessment by a technical expert. White papers need not carry official institutional signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper submission mechanics (FedConnect/SAM registration)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR white paper submissions use FedConnect; organizations applying online through FedConnect must register with SAM and receive a UEI (SAM registration must be renewed annually).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If first person in organization to register in FedConnect, the SAM MPIN is required. Create a FedConnect account. FedConnect support contact and hours are provided in the FOA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal technical proposal format
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical Proposal: 8.5 x 11 inch; 1-inch margins; single-spaced; Times New Roman, 12-point; Technical Proposal page limit = 25 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no page limitations for the budget. The FOA lists which sections are included in the 25-page count (e.g., Technical Approach/Project Narrative) and which are not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required proposal forms and PDF attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory SF-424 (R&R) family forms must be completed; files attached to the forms must be PDF, cannot contain macros, and cannot be password protected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any attachment is not a PDF, contains macros, or is password protected, it will not pass automated acceptance and must be resubmitted prior to the deadline. Electronic file name for all documents must not exceed 68 characters (including extension).

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424 field completion specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete SF-424 fields per FOA instructions (e.g., Field 4a: ONR enter 'N00014', ARO 'W36QYT', AFOSR 'FA9550'; Field 4b: include Program Office Code and Research Topic Chief formatted as specified; Field 11: include 'MURI:' at beginning of descriptive title and include ONR White Paper Tracking Number where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who fail to provide a Program Officer Code identifier may receive a notice that their proposal is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming and attachment constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Electronic file name must not exceed 68 characters; attachments must be PDF; no macros; no password protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-conforming attachments will fail automated checks and must be re-submitted in time to validate before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary data marking and legend
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must appropriately mark each page containing proprietary information and, for proposals containing data not to be disclosed, place a legend on the title page and mark each sheet of restricted data with a legend referencing the title page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOA provides exact title page legend text to use for data restrictions; the legend limits Government use outside evaluation to the extent provided in resulting award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project abstract must be publicly releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: A project abstract is required with the application and must be publicly releasable as specified in the FOA (Section II.D.2.c.(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract contains no proprietary or restricted information and is suitable for public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and representations required
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses to the Certifications and Representations indicated in Section II.F of the FOA are required with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and include all required certifications/representations at proposal submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of current and pending support
rubrics_metrics.description: This announcement requires that all current and pending research support, as defined by Section 223 of the FY21 National Defense Authorization Act, must be disclosed at the time of proposal for all covered individuals (listed as key personnel including PI/Co-PI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclosure will be updated annually during award performance and whenever covered individuals are added. Failure to report fully and completely may be considered a material statement under the False Claims Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of commitment and conflict of interest disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The funding agency may conduct a pre-award conflict of interest/conflict of commitment review of any proposal selected for funding; any significant conflict may be a basis for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should disclose conflicts in proposals. See FOA Section II.F.2.m for Organizational Conflict(s) of Interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of PI on multiple proposals/topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants contemplating using an individual as PI for more than one proposal and/or topic are strongly encouraged to contact Topic Chief(s) prior to white paper submission; PI participation in multiple proposals/topics shall be identified and must document time available and management plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support of PI participation in multiple proposals is at the discretion of the Topic Chief(s). Proposals must document how the PI will manage their time given possibility of multiple awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: This MURI competition is open only to, and proposals are to be submitted only by, U.S. institutions of higher education with degree-granting programs in science and/or engineering (including DoD institutions of higher education). UARCs that are not FFRDCs are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ineligible organizations (industry, DoD labs, FFRDCs, foreign entities) may collaborate but may not receive MURI funds directly or via subaward.

rubrics_metrics.name: No supplementation of existing projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for supplementation of existing projects will not be accepted under this FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit proposals that are merely supplements/continuations of ongoing projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost sharing policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost sharing is not expected and will not be used as a factor during the merit review; voluntary cost sharing may be considered by the Government if proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on cost sharing to improve merit review standing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of unclassified basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: The white papers and proposals submitted under this FOA are expected to address unclassified basic research (contracted fundamental research guidance applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult DoD Technical POCs to determine whether proposed effort constitutes fundamental vs. non-fundamental research; identify and describe any subcontracted unclassified research and include confirmation statements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracted fundamental research rules and prime contractor responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: ONR will follow USD(AT&L) guidance on 'contracted fundamental research'; research funded under Budget Activity 1 (Basic Research) or Budget Activity 2 performed on-campus may meet definition. Prime contractor must identify and describe subcontracted unclassified research and include a statement confirming that the work has been scoped, negotiated, and determined to be fundamental research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-fundamental research may require restrictions and DoD pre-publication review. Consult topic chiefs if classification is uncertain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument type and government involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will take the form of grants (ONR/AFOSR/ARO). For ARO submissions, awards may take the form of grants and/or cooperative agreements. Cooperative agreements imply substantial government involvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective applicants should contact Technical POCs to understand expected government involvement for cooperative agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding amounts and per-topic limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Total estimated MURI funding is approximately $200M over five years; typical annual funding per grant is up to $1.5M and awards generally follow topic-specific limits for amount and number of supported researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should discuss exceptions with Topic Chiefs during the white paper phase. Awards contingent on availability of funds, topic, and scope of proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic-specific anticipated resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Topic Description includes anticipated resources (e.g., average $1.5M/year for 5 years) and limits on number of funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow topic-specific statements (e.g., maximum faculty supported) and consult Topic Chiefs for questions or exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: HBCU/MI additional funding eligibility and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: For select topics, an additional $1.5M per topic over the 5-year MURI award is available specifically to support HBCU/MI participation; to be considered, the HBCU/MI participant must satisfy eligibility in 10 U.S.C. § 4144 and include a Department of Education eligibility letter dated in the year of application in the full proposal (strongly encouraged at white paper stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HBCU/MI team members are not required for submission; if the current eligibility letter is not submitted with the full proposal application for minority serving institutions that are not an HBCU or TCU, the application will not be considered for the additional $1.5M MURI funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PI and primary awardee institution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals shall name one Principal Investigator (PI) as the responsible technical point of contact and one institution shall be the primary awardee for award execution. The PI shall come from the primary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relationship among participating institutions and apportionment of funds, including sub-awards if any, shall be described in both the proposal text and the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward and ineligible organization funding approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Ineligible organizations may collaborate but may not receive MURI funds directly. When additional funding for an ineligible organization is necessary, such funds may be identified via a separate supplemental proposal attached to the primary MURI proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supplemental proposal will be evaluated in accordance with MURI review criteria by the Research Topic Chief and, if approved, may be funded using non-MURI or non-Government funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: White paper feedback and role of Research Topic Chiefs
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on an assessment of white papers, the responsible Research Topic Chief will provide informal feedback to prospective awardees to encourage or discourage submission of proposals and may provide feedback encouraging re-teaming to strengthen a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit white papers to minimize labor/cost of full proposals with low chance of selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational Conflicts of Interest identification
rubrics_metrics.description: White papers shall include identification of any Organizational Conflict(s) of Interest (if any) as required in Section II.F.2.m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address potential conflicts early; follow FOA guidance for disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from unauthorized disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical and budget proposals (or any other material) submitted under this FOA will not be returned and will be treated as sensitive competitive information and disclosed only for evaluation purposes in accordance with applicable law and DoD regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark proprietary pages appropriately and follow the FOA's procedures for restricted data legends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting rules for hard copy submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard copy white papers should be stapled in the upper left-hand corner; plastic covers or binders should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow agency-specific instructions for physical submissions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on types of acceptable attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate attachments such as individual brochures or reprints will not be accepted with white papers; do NOT email ZIP files and/or password protected files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep white papers self-contained within the specified page limits and required attachments only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated acceptance and resubmission risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Files that are not PDF, contain macros, or are password protected will not pass the automated acceptance check and will need to be resubmitted prior to the submission deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan submission early enough to resolve automated acceptance failures before Grants.gov validation cutoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic contact and pre-submission communication encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: It is strongly recommended that Applicants communicate with the Research Topic Chiefs regarding funding limits, team composition, and other topic-specific issues before submission of formal proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topic Chief contact information is provided in Section II.H Topic Descriptions. Discuss exceptions to topic resource limits during white paper phase.
